Validate the arguments of exported functions

Source: R/utils-checks.R
is_scalar_number.Rd

Internal argument checkers called at the top of every exported function. Each aborts with a classed rlang_error whose message names the offending argument, attributed to the exported function the user actually called (via call) rather than to the checker. They exist so a wrong argument fails with a plain message instead of an error raised from deep inside a dplyr verb or from a base R if () ("missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed").

Usage

is_scalar_number(x)

check_data_frame(x, arg = rlang::caller_arg(x), call = rlang::caller_env())

check_flag(x, arg = rlang::caller_arg(x), call = rlang::caller_env())

check_string(
  x,
  allow_null = FALSE,
  arg = rlang::caller_arg(x),
  call = rlang::caller_env()
)

check_character(
  x,
  allow_null = FALSE,
  arg = rlang::caller_arg(x),
  call = rlang::caller_env()
)

check_number(
  x,
  lower = -Inf,
  upper = Inf,
  arg = rlang::caller_arg(x),
  call = rlang::caller_env()
)

Arguments

x

The value to check.

arg

The argument name to use in the error message. Defaults to the caller's expression for x.

call

The environment the error is attributed to. Defaults to the caller's frame, i.e. the exported function.

allow_null

Logical. If TRUE, NULL passes the check.

lower, upper

Inclusive numeric bounds for check_number().

Value

is_scalar_number() returns a single logical. The check_*() functions return x invisibly when it is valid, and otherwise abort.

Details

By default arg is rlang::caller_arg(x), the expression the user passed to the calling function, so check_data_frame(ed_data) reports ed_data. is_scalar_number() is the non-aborting predicate behind check_number().
